title: Knee Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute monoarticular knee pain, fever, and chills. The knee is warm, swollen, erythematous, and exquisitely tender with limited range of motion. Disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI) is the most common cause of septic arthritis in sexually active young adults. Classic triad: tenosynovitis, dermatitis (pustular or vesiculopustular lesions), and migratory polyarthralgia progressing to monoarticular septic arthritis. Most commonly affects knee. Diagnosis: arthrocentesis with synovial fluid analysis (WBC >50,000, Gram stain may show Gram-negative diplococci, culture positive in only 50%). Also culture cervix, urethra, rectum, pharynx for N. gonorrhoeae. NAAT on synovial fluid. Treatment: ceftriaxone 1g IV daily initially, then switch to oral cefixime or fluoroquinolone based on sensitivities. If chlamydia co-infection possible (common), add doxycycline or azithromycin. Joint drainage (serial aspiration or arthroscopy). Partner treatment essential.
